learning.title: A supervisor's drain budget also bounds run()'s shutdown quiescence, so a small one makes the test race its own writes
learning.trigger: A recovery test builds a ProductionWorkerSupervisor with a small drainTimeoutMs (25 or 100 ms), drains it, and awaits run() later; or counts heartbeats until a claim stops a supervisor whose heartbeat interval is 100 ms.
learning.mistake: The budget is the drain deadline and the time run() allows the work left when it fires, and that work includes the drain's own release writes and any write the test itself starts after the deadline (several fsynced writes behind one lock, seconds on a loaded host). run() then throws WorkerShutdownQuiescenceError. If nothing observed run() yet, Deno reports an uncaught module error and cancels every later test in the file (explicit unreconciled heartbeat rejects a running attempt, 2 of 25 whole-file runs and 8 of 20 alone under 6 CPU hogs; drain quarantines every unsettled attempt before nonretryable flush stop, 13 of 30 under 4). The registration helper tests did the same at 100 ms: drain serializes an in-flight claim and gates executor start (the claim commit outlasts the deadline, so the drain heartbeat is skipped) and drain deadline aborts an unreleased claim and preserves its replay key (the claim only unwinds when the test releases it, and the release saves the pending claim key), 6 of 30 runs together under 6 CPU hogs. The two arbitrate tests that completed a settled effect during a drain kept a 2 s budget and hit the same error (settled completion at termination evidence capacity cannot resume after restart, 1 of 20 whole-file runs under 6 CPU hogs; with every fsync delayed by 250 ms the sibling settled completion during drain is quarantined across restart fails the same way, and the capacity test fails at 500 ms). A heartbeat count had the same flaw: restart sends an uncommitted heartbeat first without adopting its process session read 3 instead of 2 once the claim's writes outlasted the 100 ms interval.
learning.rule: Drain a supervisor only after its claim has settled, or give it a budget the writes fit in when the scenario does not depend on the deadline; keep a bound that proves early exit as a fraction of that budget. A test that depends on the deadline keeps it, raises it until the writes the test starts after it fit (15 s; 5 s still failed once in 80 runs), and scales its elapsed bounds by the same ratios. A heartbeat count that must stop at the claim gets a heartbeatIntervalMs the scenario never reaches. Pass every run() through observeRun (tests/helpers/worker-execution/recovery-support.ts) at creation so a rejection fails the test that awaits it. Delaying every Deno.FsFile.sync (100 ms for the registration tests, 250 to 500 ms for the arbitrate ones) reproduces all of these without CPU load.

verification.requirement: The whole arbitrate recovery file passes 40 of 40 runs under 6 CPU hogs; the base fails 2 of 25 and cancels the module.
With every fsync delayed by 100 ms the base fails the three registration helper tests above and the fixed tree passes them.

With every fsync delayed by 500 ms the base fails settled completion at termination evidence capacity cannot resume after restart at the first run() (DRAIN_DEADLINE, then the quiescence error) and the fixed tree passes that stage.
